transcript.text: LG GSXV91BSAE showing Er FF and the freezer is only about -8. There's a scraping noise and frost on the back wall inside. Help!

I have noted the ERFF/FF code on your LG freezer display. This is a controller report and does not prove a part has failed, but it is the right place to start checking why you are seeing heavy ice and frost on the back wall. Frost builds up quickly if warm, damp air gets inside the unit. Was a door left open or not shut properly recently, or did a lot of food go in at once?
Yes, the freezer door was found ajar overnight last week. The Er FF started about 2 days ago. The freezer is full too, so I'm worried about the food at -8.

[Heading: One-off frost (door / loading)]
Thanks for letting us know about that. A one-off build-up after the door was left open (or heavy loading) is normal, not a fault. Please do a full manual defrost: switch it off at the socket, move the food into cool bags, put towels down and leave the doors open until all the ice has melted (let it melt — no knives or sharp tools), then dry it and switch back on. Keep the doors shut and if the frost comes back within a few days, let me know — no part is needed.

I can't leave it off for 24 hours, there's nowhere to put a full freezer's worth of food. I could maybe do 6-8 hours overnight with the food wrapped in towels. Would that be enough? Also the scraping/ticking from the back is still there.

[Heading: One-off frost (door / loading)]
A one-off build-up after a door was left open (or heavy loading) is normal and not a fault. Please carry out a full manual defrost. Switch the appliance off at the socket, move food into cool bags, lay down towels, and leave the doors open until all ice has melted naturally—do not use knives or sharp tools to remove it. Once clear, dry the interior thoroughly and switch the unit back on. Keep the doors shut during normal use. If frost returns within a few days, please let me know; no part is needed in this instance.
